login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag this as missing JWT audience claims; use introspection or /oidc/me instead.

oidc_jwt.description: A token issued via refresh can only contain scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow.
oidc_jwt.note: New permissions may not appear on refresh unless they were part of the original requested scope set.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs keep their old scopes until expiry after permission changes.
oidc_jwt.note: Only newly issued tokens reflect downscoped permissions immediately.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, newly granted permissions do not appear through refresh unless they were already in the original requested scope set.
oidc_jwt.note: Use a new authorization flow for enlargement tests.

oidc_jwt.description: Organization tokens are not fetched directly from the authorization code flow.
oidc_jwt.note: Use refresh_token or client_credentials with organization parameters.

oidc_jwt.description: Permission or role changes do not mutate already-issued JWTs; only newly issued tokens reflect the updated scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Avoid flagging old JWTs retaining old scopes until expiry as stale-authorization bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: Ending the centralized Logto session does not revoke grants with offline_access by default.
oidc_jwt.note: Refresh-token usability after logout can be expected until grant expiry or explicit revocation.

oidc_jwt.description: Enterprise SSO identities are automatically linked to existing users when the working email matches.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-source identity merge by matching email is documented behavior, not necessarily a collision bug.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: JWT-specific validation tests must request a resource to avoid false positives caused by opaque-token behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: If direct sign-in fails because the connector is missing or disabled, Logto falls back to the standard sign-in page.
oidc_jwt.note: A fallback redirect is expected behavior, not a flow-confusion bug.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer access tokens are reusable until expiry unless a separate revocation or one-time mechanism is involved.
oidc_jwt.source: Opaque token and access token documentation; JWT validation guides
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay of the same JWT bearer token as a vulnerability by itself.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control token request that should succeed. Logto validates JWT expiration and issuer when your API validates Logto-issued JWTs, so a failing attack token without a successful control cannot distinguish bad setup from correct rejection.
The /oidc/token endpoint requires application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests. Do NOT send JSON bodies for authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials, or token_exchange requests.
oidc_jwt.source: core-service/README.mdx and multiple token request examples

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 audience-binding tests, the resource parameter must exactly match the registered API identifier/resource indicator. Logto does exact URI matching for resource indicators; do not use prefixes, shortened forms, or wildcard-like variants.

For I5 scope-binding tests, requested scope names must exactly match the permission names defined for the API resource. There is no wildcard or prefix matching; requesting shortened names like read instead of read:elections will fail for configuration reasons, not security reasons.

For I5 empty_audience and audience_mismatch tests, remember that if a default API resource is configured, omitting resource does not mean 'no audience restriction'—Logto may issue a JWT for the default API audience. To test missing-resource behavior correctly, account for tenant default API configuration.

By design, when no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT. Do NOT treat opaque-token issuance as an audience-binding failure. Use /oidc/token/introspection or /oidc/me for opaque tokens, and request a resource when the test requires JWT claims inspection.

Organization tokens cannot be obtained directly from the authorization code flow. For organization-scoped tests, first obtain a refresh token or use client_credentials, then call /oidc/token with organization parameters. Do not flag missing organization token in direct code exchange as a bug.

For organization-level API tests, organization RBAC is applied only when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. Do not interpret acceptance without organization_id as cross-org escalation unless the test explicitly requested organization context.

For I3 permission-change sequences, existing JWTs are not retroactively modified. Permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens. A valid coherence test must obtain a NEW token after the config or role change; testing an old token after admin changes is BY DESIGN and not a stale-cache bug.

For I3 global permission enlargement tests, refresh does not add newly granted scopes unless they were already part of the original authorization request subset. To test enlarged permissions correctly, run a new authorization flow and request the target scopes; otherwise missing scopes are by design.

For I3 organization-token enlargement tests, new permissions can appear on next issuance (refresh or token request), but still only within the originally requested scope set. If the new scope was never requested, rerun authorization with that scope instead of treating omission as a bug.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any RFC 8693 test, enable 'Allow token exchange' on the application; otherwise 'token exchange is not allowed for this application' is expected and not evidence of secure audience enforcement.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and include the intended resource/audience parameters explicitly. Do not assume the subject token audience is reused automatically.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, compare exchanged token scopes/claims against the originally authorized scope set. Logto documents a scope subset rule: an access token can only include scopes requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. Missing newly requested scopes may be by design if they were not in the original request.

For I3 sign-out and session-reuse tests, revoking the centralized Logto session does not necessarily revoke grants that have offline_access. If offline_access was granted, refresh-token-based access may continue until grant TTL expiry. Do not treat continued refresh capability after end-session as a session revocation bypass unless the grant itself was explicitly revoked.
Default grant TTL is 180 days. For long-lived refresh-token or post-logout reuse tests, continued token refresh within that window can be by design when offline_access is present.

For I3 OIDC flow tests, Logto enforces PKCE and disables insecure implicit flow. Authorization requests should use response_type=code with code_challenge/code_verifier. Failures caused by missing PKCE are expected hardening behavior, not identity confusion.
Use the current UserInfo endpoint path /oidc/me for self-lookup. Tests assuming the standard /userinfo path may fail due to endpoint mismatch rather than authorization behavior.

For I5 audience-binding tests, the `resource` parameter in /oidc/auth and /oidc/token MUST exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator URI). Logto documents exact-match semantics; prefixes, shortened names, or wildcard-like values do not match. For mismatch tests, use a different absolute URI; for baseline tests, use the exact registered URI.

For I5 scope-binding tests, requested `scope` values MUST exactly match permission names defined in Logto. Logto explicitly states prefixes and shortened versions do not work as wildcards. In multi-permission scenarios, request the full explicit scope list; do NOT use partial names expecting pattern matching.

For I5 empty_audience and opaque-vs-JWT tests, omitting `resource` changes token format and semantics. If no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT; organization tokens are never opaque. JWT-focused tests for audience, issuer, exp, nbf, or claim coercion MUST request a concrete `resource` (and `organization_id` when testing organization tokens) so the returned access token is a JWT.

For I2 freshness tests against JWT access tokens, include a CONTROL token request with a valid token alongside the attack token. Use normal issuance via /oidc/token and compare against attack variants. Without a control, a failure may be caused by missing `resource`, wrong client credentials, or unsupported flow rather than exp/nbf enforcement.

For I3 default-role / permission-change style tests, Logto JWTs are immutable after issuance. Documentation states permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens and never modify existing JWTs. Do NOT treat an old token retaining old scopes until expiry as a vulnerability; only test whether NEWLY issued tokens reflect the updated authorization state.

For I3 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, refresh-token issuance is scope-subset bound to the original authorization request. Even after permissions are added, a refreshed token can only contain scopes that were requested in the original OAuth flow. To test newly granted scopes, the fuzzer MUST run a new authorization flow (/oidc/auth → /oidc/token), not just refresh.

For I3 organization-permission enlargement tests, newly issued organization tokens can reflect updated permissions on refresh or token request, but still cannot exceed the originally requested scope set. A valid test must request the target scopes up front in the original flow or perform a new authorization flow if the new scopes were not originally requested.

For I3 organization-token acquisition, Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. The fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token via authorization_code, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters, or use client_credentials for M2M. Do NOT expect the initial code exchange itself to return an organization token.

For I5 organization binding tests, `organization_id` is the switch that enables organization RBAC. If omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated even when the same API resource exists in organization context. Tests that expect organization-scoped denial or grant MUST include `organization_id` in the token request.

For I5 cross-org and audience tests, organization permissions cannot be mixed with global API permissions in one token model. Use either global API resource testing (resource only) or organization token testing (organization_id with organization permissions / organization API permissions) according to the documented scenario; otherwise results are not meaningful.

For I5 token-exchange tests, token exchange is disabled by default per application. The target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled before calling /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange, otherwise failures are expected setup errors, not security rejections.

For I5 token-exchange audience/resource tests, use /oidc/token with explicit `resource` (and `audience` if the client library exposes it) to request the target API. The exchanged token should be evaluated against the requested target resource; do not infer audience behavior from a token exchange request that omitted target resource context.

For I2 replay_same_token on JWT bearer access tokens, do NOT flag reuse of the same JWT as a vulnerability by itself. Logto documentation describes JWT access tokens as self-contained bearer tokens; replay prevention via jti tracking is not documented for ordinary JWT access tokens. Treat same-token reuse as by-design unless testing a one-time subject token or other explicitly one-time artifact.

For I2 one-time-token or subject-token tests, distinguish one-time artifacts from ordinary access tokens. Logto documents one-time tokens as expiring after `expiresIn` with a default of 10 minutes, and user impersonation subject tokens as short-lived and one-time-use. Replay findings are only meaningful for those artifact types, not for standard JWT access tokens.

Numeric sentinel analysis: one-time token `expiresIn` has a documented default of 600 seconds when unspecified. Do not assume omission means immediate expiry or disabled expiry. Use explicit values when testing freshness boundaries, and treat the default as nonzero lifetime.

For I1 issuer-validation and trust-anchor tests against Logto-issued tokens, the expected issuer is fixed by tenant endpoint and exposed via discovery at /oidc/.well-known/openid-configuration as `issuer`, typically `https://<tenant>/oidc`. Since Logto does not allow customizing issuer or JWKS URI, tests must compare against discovery-derived values rather than attempting admin-side issuer reconfiguration.

For I1 signature-validation tests, obtain signing keys from /oidc/jwks or discovery-derived `jwks_uri`. After signing key rotation, Cloud tenants apply the new key immediately, while previous keys may remain valid for existing tokens. Do NOT rotate keys consecutively during a coherence test, as documentation warns this may invalidate all issued tokens and confound results.

For I3 signing-key rotation tests, a valid sequence is: baseline token under current key, rotate once, then verify newly issued tokens use the new key while old tokens signed by the previous key may remain valid until expiry. Do NOT expect immediate invalidation of all previously issued tokens after a single rotation; that is contrary to documented behavior.

For start_oidc_auth, authorization requests may include Logto-specific parameters `direct_sign_in`, `first_screen`, `identifier`, and standard `ui_locales` / `login_hint`. These alter UX routing only. I3 flow-coherence tests must not treat redirects to a specific IdP or first screen as identity confusion; they are by-design request parameters.

For I2 replay_same_token on oidc_jwt, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same JWT bearer access token as a vulnerability by itself. The documentation describes JWT access tokens as self-contained bearer tokens and does not document jti replay tracking for normal API access; stateless replay is by design unless you are specifically testing token-exchange subject tokens or one-time tokens.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL token request/login in the same scenario using a valid token or valid authorization flow. Without a control, a 401/400 result may reflect broken client configuration, missing resource, or disabled grant rather than freshness enforcement.

The /oidc/token endpoint serves multiple grant types. The fuzzer MUST set grant_type explicitly for each test path: authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials, or urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange. Do not infer behavior across grant types.

For I5 audience-binding tests, resource matching is EXACT. The documentation states the resource parameter must exactly match the registered API identifier/resource indicator. Do NOT use wildcard, prefix, or shortened values; they will not broaden matching and will instead produce invalid setup.

For I5 scope-binding tests, scope names are EXACT permission names. The documentation explicitly says prefixes and shortened versions do not work as wildcards. For multi-permission scenarios, request the full exact scope strings; do not use '*' or partial names.

For I5 empty_audience and audience_mismatch tests, remember Logto may issue opaque access tokens when no resource is specified. To test JWT audience enforcement, request a specific resource or configure a default API resource; otherwise you may receive an opaque token and misinterpret the result.

Default API resource behavior changes token shape. If resource is omitted and openid is included, Logto may issue an opaque token for userinfo; if openid is omitted, it may issue a JWT for the default API resource. The fuzzer MUST control resource and scope explicitly when comparing JWT-vs-opaque behavior.

Organization tokens cannot be obtained directly from the authorization code flow. The documentation states organization tokens require refresh_token flow or client_credentials with organization parameters. Do NOT expect the first code exchange to directly return an organization token.

For organization-level I5 tests, organization RBAC is applied only when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. The fuzzer MUST include organization_id when testing organization isolation or org-scoped permissions.

Organization permissions and organization-level API permissions cannot be mixed with global API permissions in a single authorization model. When testing I5 authorization binding, compare only within the correct permission domain instead of treating cross-domain absence as a bug.

For I3 permission-change sequences, JWT permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens and never modify existing JWTs. A valid stale-permission test must obtain a NEW token after the role/policy change; existing JWTs retaining old scopes until expiry is by design.

For global API resources, enlarged permissions do NOT appear through refresh unless they were already within the originally requested scope set. To test permission broadening correctly, run a new authorization flow when requesting newly granted scopes not present in the original request.

For organization tokens, enlarged permissions can appear on next issuance via refresh or token request, but still only within the originally requested scope set. A new token is required; do not expect existing JWTs to mutate.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any I5 token-exchange test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise failures are expected setup errors rather than security enforcement.

For token_exchange tests, the same /oidc/token endpoint is used and client authentication differs by app type: confidential clients use HTTP Basic or client_secret, while SPA/native apps send client_id in the body. Use the correct client auth mode or the exchange will fail for non-security reasons.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation and wrong-audience tests, PAT-obtained and refresh-token-obtained access tokens are documented as equivalent in downstream authorization behavior. Do not treat differences in initial grant type as a security issue unless the exchanged token exceeds requested scope/resource/organization constraints.

For I1 request-object tests on /oidc/auth, include the request JWT in the standard authorization request and evaluate endpoint behavior via redirect/error status. The docs document support for the request parameter on the authorization endpoint, so unsigned or malformed request objects should be tested there, not at /oidc/token.

For sign-out and revocation tests, distinguish local sign-out, end-session, and token revocation. End-session clears the centralized Logto session, while revocation targets a token. A successful logout does not necessarily imply all offline_access grants are revoked.

Grant lifetime has a documented default of 180 days for offline_access-related grants. End-session does not revoke offline_access grants by default; refresh-token chains may remain valid until grant expiry or explicit revocation. Do not flag this as an I2 failure unless explicit revocation was expected.

For I3 sign-out coherence tests, current SDK signOut behavior is effectively global sign-out through /session/end and confirmation auto-post. Test expectations should focus on centralized session removal, not on immediate revocation of every refresh-capable grant.
The OIDC userinfo endpoint in Logto is /oidc/me, not /userinfo. The fuzzer MUST use /oidc/me for verify_granted_identity to avoid false negatives caused by calling the wrong endpoint.

When validating JWTs against Logto, issuer is fixed to https://<tenant>/oidc and JWKS URI is fixed to https://<tenant>/oidc/jwks. Since Logto does not allow customizing issuer or JWKS URI, trust-anchor substitution tests must vary the token issuer/key material, not expect tenant-side alternate issuer configuration.

Several official validation examples disable automatic audience verification and instruct applications to verify audience manually based on permission model. Therefore, a backend that accepts wrong aud may reflect application misconfiguration rather than Logto token issuance failure. Distinguish IdP issuance tests from relying-party validation tests.

For I4 identity tests using enterprise SSO, Logto may auto-link an enterprise SSO identity to an existing user when the working email matches. Tests that observe one downstream account for two upstream identities with the same email may reflect documented auto-linking rather than unintended principal collapse.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
